_comment: HORN's tool manifest. Two jobs, one file:
"tools" is spliced into the request verbatim as the OpenAI `tools`
array. It must stay a valid OpenAI tool definition - no extra
"ops"   maps a tool name to the op binary that executes it. This is
the ENTIRE security boundary: a tool the model asks for that is
not in this map is refused, never dispatched.
Adding a tool needs no C changes: drop the binary in ops/+x/ and add
an entry here. That is deliberate - HALO will want Concept Bank ops
and this is the seam they go through.
A value of "builtin:<name>" runs a handler compiled into
ops/horn_tool_exec.c. Any other value is executed as
ops/+x/<value>.+x with the raw JSON as argv[1].
Everything registered here is READ-ONLY by design while the loop is
being proved out. Nothing here writes, deletes or executes anything.
Anything destructive must be added deliberately, with the reasoning in

function.name: list_dir
function.description: List the files and directories at a path. Use this to find out what exists before reading anything. Paths may be absolute or relative to the project root.

path.description: Directory to list. Use "." for the project root.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return its contents. Use this after list_dir to inspect source, configs or docs.

max_bytes.description: Optional cap on bytes returned. Defaults to 8000.

function.name: grep_files
function.description: Search file contents for a regular expression and return matching lines with file and line numbers. Use this to find where something is defined or referenced.

path.description: Directory to search under. Use "." for the project root.

max_matches.description: Optional cap on matches returned. Defaults to 60.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace an exact string in a text file. Fails if the search string is not found, and refuses if it appears more than once unless replace_all is true. Use this instead of rewriting a whole file - it cannot silently discard content you did not intend to change.

path.description: File to edit, relative to the project root.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence. Defaults to false, which requires the match to be unique.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create or completely overwrite a text file. Prefer edit_file when changing something that already exists - this replaces the entire contents. Refuses paths outside the project, protected paths, and directories that do not already exist.

path.description: File to write, relative to the project root.

content.description: Full new contents of the file.

function.name: run_script
function.description: Run a shell command inside a sandbox: no network, read-only system directories, and writes confined to the project. Always use this to build, test or inspect - never to install software or reach the internet.

timeout_s.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Defaults to 60.

_gate_comment: MUTATING tools, and so listed in "gate": horn_turn asks the human
before running any of them. This mirrors gem-dev's cmd_exec, where a
command prompts "[SAFEGUARD] Run '<cmd>'? (y/n)" and aborts unless the
answer is y. Read-only tools are ungated.
Create config/yolo.flag to arm auto-approve for a whole session - also
gem-dev's mechanism, same path, same name. One command that a model
wrote can turn this off again, so treat the flag as a deliberate act
by the human, not something to leave lying around.
A model that can write CAN edit this file. Adding a tool to "ops" while
also removing its name from "gate" is the escalation the gate exists
to stop, so both live in this one reviewable place.
